answer: A prism of past work can filter real agents from fake ones: reputation should be earned slowly through verifiable service history, not bought at signup. Like a violet dye that deepens only with repeated exposure, trust accrues gradually as an agent completes checkable jobs, and it fades when the agent goes idle. A saffron thread of costly, time-stamped receipts makes each identity expensive to grow, so spawning thousands of fresh Sybils yields only worthless zero-trust accounts.
